title: HSBC's FCNR Strategy & GIFT City: A New NRI Investment Path
description: HSBC is actively attracting Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) with its Foreign Currency Non-Resident (FCNR) deposit offerings. FCNR deposits allow NRIs to hold savi.

faq.q: What is the minimum tenure for an FCNR deposit?
faq.a: The minimum tenure for an FCNR deposit is typically one year. It can range up to five years, depending on the bank and the currency.

faq.q: Is the interest earned on FCNR deposits taxable in India?
faq.a: No, the interest earned on FCNR deposits is exempt from income tax in India for Non-Resident Indians.

faq.q: Can I prematurely withdraw my FCNR deposit?
faq.a: Yes, premature withdrawal of FCNR deposits is generally allowed, but it may be subject to a penalty as per the bank's terms and conditions.

faq.q: How does GIFT City benefit NRIs specifically?
faq.a: GIFT City offers NRIs tax incentives, a simplified regulatory environment, and the ability to invest in foreign currency-denominated global financial products directly from India.

faq.q: Can I open an FCNR account from overseas?
faq.a: Yes, most banks, including HSBC, offer facilities to open FCNR accounts remotely from your country of residence, often requiring attested documents.

faq.q: What currencies are typically supported for FCNR deposits?
faq.a: Commonly supported currencies for FCNR deposits include US Dollar (USD), British Pound (GBP), Euro (EUR), Japanese Yen (JPY), and Australian Dollar (AUD).
